reader.requirement: At --std 85 THROUGH and THRU must be the same word in an EVALUATE selection object: either spelling builds the same inclusive range object.
reader.edition-search: grep THRU|THROUGH in the grammar and the reserved-word table: one token pair, no edition arm; WhenPhraseBinder.cs#BindRangeObject reads the parse node, not the word

probes.printed: R1 OK (WHEN 1 THRU 5 rejected, WHEN 6 THROUGH 9 selected), R10 OK (7 THRU 7 ALSO "A" THRU "C")
probes.expected: both spellings form the same inclusive range

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.13.3 SR3  (║6.13.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR3

reader.notes: Re-read after kb/Work PB2338: the range binder moved from EvaluateBinder to WhenPhraseBinder unchanged; the grammar's valueRange takes either token, and nothing downstream sees which was written.

refuter.evidence: rfthru-001 (exit 0): THROUGH in an ALSO set, after NOT, over a figurative LOW-VALUE and between arithmetic expressions (N - 1 THROUGH N + 1) behaves exactly as THRU in the same statement (T1, T2, T3 OK). 'OK  §1985:VI.6.13.3 SR3  (║6.13.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR3'
